question.text: When photon of energy <math><mn>4.0</mn><mi></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> strikes the surface of a metal <math><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the ejected photoelectrons have maximum kinetic energy <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> and de-Broglie wavelength <math><msub><mrow><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo>.</mo></math> The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons liberated from another metal <math><mi>B</mi></math> by photon of energy <math><mn>4.50</mn><mi></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> is <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo>-</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo>.</mo></math> If the de-Broglie wavelength of these photoelectrons <math><msub><mrow><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mrow><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></math> then the work function of metal <math><mi>B</mi></math> is:

solution.text:
Relation between de-Broglie wavelength and K.E. is
λ=h2(KE)me⇒λ∝1KE
λAλB=KEBKEA
⇒12=TA-1.5TA⇒TA=2 eV
∴KEB=2-1.5=0.5 eV
ϕB=4.5-0.5=4 eV
